text: The subject, Tariq Tariq, a low‑risk grocery wholesaler, received an unusually high volume of cash deposits at the Hyderabad Main Branch between 4 July and 28 July 2026. In the 30‑day period the account was credited with more than PKR 45 million in cash, including nine deposits exceeding PKR 2 million (e.g., PKR 2 507 000 on 4 July, PKR 2 467 000 on 6 July, PKR 3 109 000 on 9 July, PKR 3 492 000 on 13 July, PKR 3 557 000 on 16 July, PKR 2 727 000 on 20 July, PKR 3 479 000 on 28 July). The typology engine flagged the activity (score 320, above the alert threshold of 300) for “30‑day cash credits exceed the 90‑day baseline” and “high count of cash deposits”. The cash inflows were immediately followed by three identical outbound IBFT transfers of PKR 8 119 000 each to the same counterparty, Metro FMCG Distributors (account PK**BAHL****5521 at Synthetic Bank C) on 7, 14, 21 and 28 July. The repeated large outflows to a single supplier, without supporting documentation beyond generic “STOCK INVOICE” memos, together with the pattern of large cash deposits, are inconsistent with the declared monthly turnover (PKR 71 million) and the subject’s stated occupation. These characteristics suggest possible structuring or layering of illicit funds, warranting the filing of a Suspicious Transaction Report.
